nodes.body: <<FILL role=setup words=75 beats='the Ninth Sword rides into Gallowmere in freezing rain under a commission seal; a stockade town on the Barrow Moor, the Warden's tower lit, the muster yard full of rival companies, Dellach counting the competition, Nyre reading the gate notice, Kettle too quiet'>>

choices.label: Report to the Warden-Marshal at once.
Take the company into the Broken Wheel first.
Walk the muster yard and see who else is hiring.
Let Nyre take you to the Ledger counting room.
Ask Kettle what she is not saying about the moor.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='Warden-Marshal Ansel Redd lays out the commission: the winter tax-iron of the Kar Duhn garrison never came down the road, and neither did the garrison; sixty crowns for the iron and the pay-ledger both, and no Warden will go in with you'>>

choices.label: Ask what actually happened to the garrison.
Press him for better terms before you sign.
Sign it as written and be done.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='Redd's answer is thin and he knows it: two relief patrols turned back at the barrow gate for reasons neither could write down, the second came back nine men short, and the vault door was found standing open a hand's width'>>

choices.label: Press him for better terms now that you know.
Sign anyway; the coin is the coin.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the haggle in a cold office: Redd has no more coin, but he has a charter, a stamped writ of salvage that would make the Ninth Sword a name instead of a hired knife, and he offers it only if you drop the hazard pay'>>

choices.label: Take the charter and drop the hazard pay.
Take the coin; charters do not feed anyone.
Refuse the whole insult and ride south.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='the writ of salvage stamped and sanded, Redd's clerk recording the Ninth Sword by name for the first time; Dellach says nothing and stands a little straighter, Nyre notes what it cost'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the contract signed, and Redd's last condition spoken quietly: bring back the pay-ledger even if you cannot bring back the iron, because the ledger is what the Marshal's own account will be measured against'>>

choices.label: Ask him for a guide across the moor.
Ask to read the garrison's last dispatch.
Go and gather your company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=50 beats='the only guide willing is Bram Sull, a fen-runner with a drinker's hands who wants a full share and swears he has walked the dykes in fog; Kettle looks at him the way you look at weather coming'>>

choices.label: Hire him out of the advance.
Refuse; Kettle knows the moor better than she admits.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='Bram hired and already spending his share, Dellach unimpressed, Kettle openly disgusted; the company is five now, and one of the five is a stranger who talks'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='the garrison's last dispatch, water-stained, in a clerk's failing hand: routine counts, routine weather, and then a final line that is not routine at all, that the ninth hand is missing and the door will not hold at eight'>>

choices.label: Take that with you and gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the Broken Wheel: peat smoke, wet wool, three companies drinking on other people's commissions, a charcoal burner telling anyone who will listen about lamps moving on the moor in file, and a Rooks bravo already measuring Dellach'>>

choices.label: Buy the room a round and listen.
Corner the charcoal burner about the lamps.
Get between Dellach and the Rooks bravo.
Take the company upstairs; sleep is worth more.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='a round bought and the room loosening: the garrison paid its own wages nine times over on paper, a Ledger factor came up from the south twice this autumn, and nobody in Gallowmere will take a contract past the barrow gate at any price'>>

choices.label: Follow up the lamps story.
You have heard enough for one night.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the charcoal burner sober enough to be precise: lamps in a file of nine, always nine, moving along the old dwarf road at the same hour, and stopping at the barrow gate as if waiting to be counted in'>>

choices.label: Pay him for the whole story, slowly.
Write him off as drink and firelight.
Have him walk you out to see the lamps tonight.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the rest of it for two coppers: the lamps have come every ninth night since midsummer, the burner's brother followed them once, and what came back to the hut was his brother's coat, folded, with the buttons cut off'>>

choices.label: Let him go and gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the Rooks bravo, Corrow's man, has decided the Ninth Sword is a joke worth telling loudly; Dellach's hand is already flat on the table and the room has gone quiet enough to hear the fire'>>

choices.label: Let Dellach settle it with fists.
Pull rank and buy the man's drink.
Draw steel in a Warden town.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='three fast exchanges and the bravo folded over a bench, Dellach's knuckles split, the room's opinion of the company revised upward and its opinion of the Rooks revised down; Nyre binds the hand without comment'>>

choices.label: Get the company upstairs before it starts again.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='a bought drink, a hard smile, and the bravo backing off calling it courtesy; Dellach thinks you spent coin on nothing, Kettle thinks you bought the only thing worth having, which is a quiet night'>>

choices.label: Take the stairs and the quiet night.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='one night in a real bed above a warm floor, boots off, the company sleeping like paid soldiers instead of hunted ones; you wake before the bell feeling the difference in your hands'>>

choices.label: Gather the company at first light.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the muster yard in the rain: two companies loading out, a Rooks banner over the best dry ground, and a handful of loose hands looking for a fourth-share, among them a woman in a salt-stained coat reading sigils off a wagon axle'>>

choices.label: Talk to the woman reading sigils.
Hire the two spear-brothers who ask for little.
Cross the yard to the Rooks banner.
Hire nobody; four mouths is enough.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='Ilsabet Crane, hedge-thaumaturge, glass and salt and a burned sleeve, who reads the wagon's warding aloud and then tells you plainly that whatever emptied Kar Duhn was let in, not broken in, because the marks on the relief patrol's shields were made from the inside'>>

choices.label: Take her on at a full share.
Offer her half a share and see if she takes it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='a full share agreed with a handshake she does not let go of until you meet her eye; she owns one crate, and everything in it is written on rather than made of anything, and Kettle helps her carry it without being asked'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='half a share taken with a shrug that costs you something you cannot price yet; she comes, she works, and she keeps one hand's worth of what she knows in reserve, which is exactly what you paid for'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the spear-brothers, Odd and Sten, cheap and cheerful and entirely untested; they ask about the coin twice and the moor not once, and Dellach hires them because a shield wall of two is not a shield wall'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=50 beats='Captain Vasse Corrow of the Rooks, dry under an oiled awning, offering to buy your commission outright for forty crowns and calling it mercy; she has been to the barrow gate and she will not say what turned her around'>>

choices.label: Refuse, and drink with her long enough to learn why.
Take the forty crowns and live.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='Corrow drinks and talks around it: her scout went in at the gate and came out wrong, counting under her breath, and would not stop counting until she died of it eleven days later in a Ledger hospice'>>

choices.label: Leave her the awning and gather your company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the Ledger counting room, warm as a church and quieter, where Factor Halloway keeps the frontier's debts in a hand like engraving; Nyre's order and his are the same order, which is why she does not trust him'>>

choices.label: Have Nyre read the garrison's pay account.
Borrow against the commission for better kit.
Hear out the contract Halloway would rather offer.
Leave; Ledger business is her business.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='the account read aloud in Nyre's flat voice: the Kar Duhn garrison drew its winter pay nine times in nine years and every draw was signed by a different hand, and the ninth signature is a mark, not a name'>>

choices.label: Take that with you.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='credit against the commission spent well: oil, dry powder, two lamps with clean wicks, a new haft for Dellach's poleaxe, and salt enough for Ilsabet to work with; the debt sits behind you like a second contract'>>

choices.label: Load out and gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=50 beats='Halloway's better offer, laid out with real kindness: forget the iron, bring him the ledger alone, and the Ledger will carry the company's debts for nine years, term for term, hand for hand'>>

choices.label: Sign what Halloway is actually offering.
Refuse, and note that he used the word nine.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='Kettle on the rampart with her back to the moor, lying badly about why she chose this contract; she was born in the fens under that hill and she has not said the words Kar Duhn once since Gallowmere came in sight'>>

choices.label: Press her, gently, until she says it.
Let her keep it; everyone is owed one silence.
Tell the Marshal she is holding something back.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the truth in pieces: she went under the hill at eleven with her father's crew, they were paid in silence and salt to carry crates down and nothing up, and she is the only one of that crew still walking'>>

choices.label: Ask what the crews sang down there.
That is enough for tonight.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the counting rhyme the crews used on the stair, which Kettle recites without expression: nine hands on the iron, nine irons in the door, eight to hold it shut, and the ninth to keep the score'>>

choices.label: Sit with that a while, then gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the Marshal informed, the Marshal pleased, a note made in a Warden ledger about a captain who reports; Kettle is on the wagon at dawn and does not look at you for two days, and the company notices which way you jumped'>>

choices.label: Gather the company.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the last hour in Gallowmere with the company assembled in the yard, kit checked, the moor going blue-black past the stockade, and the only question left the shape of your leaving'>>

choices.label: March at first light, light kit, good order.
March tonight in the rain, ahead of the Rooks.
Spend the advance properly before you move.
Sell the commission on and be a live coward.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='out at first light with the bell, light kit and good order, the stockade gate closing behind the last man and the moor opening ahead like a held breath'>>

choices.label: Take the causeway.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='a night march in horizontal rain to steal a day on the Rooks, four miles of it, and by the time the sky greys the company is wet through and paying for the head start in the only currency that matters out here'>>

choices.label: Take the causeway.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=50 beats='the advance on the table and a morning to spend it: the mule-and-salt argument between Nyre and Dellach, one buying endurance and the other buying edge, and both of them right'>>

choices.label: Mule, salt, oil, and rope.
A moor-iron blade and a warded haft.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='a bad-tempered mule named Preacher, four stone of salt, oil, and eighty feet of tarred rope; the company jokes about the mule and will stop joking about it within the week'>>

choices.label: Take the causeway.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=45 beats='moor-iron bought off a smith who would not meet your eye: a short heavy blade and a warded haft for Dellach, cold in the hand and worth what it cost if half the stories are true'>>

choices.label: Take the causeway.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the causeway out of Gallowmere at the edge of the Barrow Moor, the last dry ground under the company's boots, three ways ahead: the drover track along the dykes, the straight line across open moor, and the dwarf road that goes under the hill and comes out nobody knows where'>>

choices.label: Take the drover track along the dykes.
Cut straight across the moor and save a day.
Follow the old dwarf road under the hill.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=failure words=50 beats='the ride south out of Gallowmere with pride intact and nothing else, the Rooks' banner going up over the commission you refused, and Dellach saying the thing you already know: that pride does not winter well'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=60 beats='out on the moor at night behind a drunk with a rushlight, the file of lamps closer than it looked and stopping to count, the burner running, and the last thing the company hears being a number said aloud in a voice that has no throat behind it'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=55 beats='steel drawn in a Warden town and the whole company in the stockade cells by midnight, the commission struck and handed to the Rooks at dawn, Redd's clerk reading the forfeiture out loud through the bars while Corrow waits in the yard'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=50 beats='forty crowns split five ways in a wet yard and the Rooks riding out with your paper; the company is alive and paid and finished as a company, because the story that gets told is the one where you sold'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=55 beats='Halloway's ink dry on nine years of the company's labour, the iron forgotten, the ledger promised, and Nyre walking out of the counting room without a word because she has read what you signed and you have not'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=50 beats='the commission sold on cheap and the road south taken before the weather turns, the moor behind you keeping its garrison and its iron, and the question of what happened under that hill following the company down every road it takes after'>>

<<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the drover track on the dyke crest, peat water on both sides going the colour of strong tea, sheep skulls set on posts every hundred paces by somebody who wanted them counted, and the hill of Kar Duhn a grey knuckle on the skyline'>>

choices.label: Keep to the dyke crest, single file.
Drop to the drove road below the bank.
Stop at the gibbet cage where the tracks cross.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the crest in a crosswind that makes every man walk like a drunk, good sightlines and no cover at all, and Dellach's flat observation that anything watching the moor has watched you for two hours'>>

choices.label: Press on to the sluice.
Get down out of sight below the bank.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the drove road below the bank, shin-deep and sucking, the mule fighting every yard and Odd going down twice; cover from the wind bought with the company's legs'>>

choices.label: Climb out at the sluice.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='a Warden's gibbet at the track crossing with a man still in it, tarred and long past complaining, and cut into the post below him a mark that is not Warden work: a ring of nine strokes with the ninth struck through'>>

choices.label: Cut the mark out of the post for Ilsabet.
Leave it be; a hanged man is a hanged man.
Camp under it, out of the wind, and move at first light.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the mark chiselled free and turned over in Ilsabet's hands, her verdict careful: not a ward, not a curse, a tally, and whoever keeps this tally has been keeping it on Warden property for a long time'>>

choices.label: Pocket it and go on to the sluice.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the dwarf sluice at the moor's throat, a cut stone channel with its gate broken half-open, black water shooting through the gap loud enough to talk over, and the track drowned for forty feet on the far side'>>

choices.label: Rope a line and wade it.
Go round by the reed island and lose an hour.
Have Ilsabet freeze the gap shut long enough to cross.
Cross dry along the gate's iron beam.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=50 beats='chest-deep in water cold enough to stop a heart, the rope line humming, Dellach's shoulders taking the strain on the far bank while Kettle counts everyone through by name'>>

choices.label: Keep the line taut and go one at a time.
Let the line go and swim the last of it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='an hour lost going round by the reed island, dry to the knee and no more, and at the island's high point the first clear sight of nine lamp hooks on the barrow gate, all of them full'>>

choices.label: Rejoin the track and make camp.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='salt and glass and Ilsabet's flat working voice, the gap crusting over in grey lace that holds for ninety seconds; the company crosses dry and she sits down hard on the far side and will not be helped up'>>

choices.label: Give her a minute, then make camp.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the open moor, pale tussock and black pool, no track and no horizon that stays put, the kind of country that is flat until it kills you; somewhere ahead the hill, and between here and it a day of guessing'>>

choices.label: Keep to the tussock lines and go slow.
Push hard and straight and save the daylight.
Follow the fresh path somebody else cut through it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the slow way, Kettle reading the tussocks like a page and calling each step, the company strung out and patient, four miles bought with six hours and nobody wet above the knee'>>

choices.label: Cut peat for the fire at the old workings.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the fast way, which works until Sten goes in to the chest and the moor takes his spear and one boot as payment, and the company spends its saved hour hauling him out by the belt'>>

choices.label: Slow down; the moor made its point.
Keep the pace and let the moor try again.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='a path cut through the tussocks days old and wide as a wagon, except no wagon made it: something was dragged this way, in quantity, and the drag marks have small hard footprints on both sides of them'>>

choices.label: Follow it and see what was dragged.
Get off it and back to open moor.
Set an ambush on the path and wait.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the butchering ground at the path's end: Warden kit stacked by type, boots in one pile and belts in another, the relief patrol's shields with the paint scraped off, and the tidiness of it worse than the smell'>>

choices.label: Take the Warden signet and the dispatch case.
Bury what can be buried and let Nyre say the words.
Back away now; the Fenkin are still close.
Follow the small footprints home.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='a Warden signet and a leather dispatch case lifted from the pile, the case still sealed, the seal not Warden but Ledger, and Nyre's face when she recognises the factor's stamp on it'>>

choices.label: Get off the path and go to ground.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='an hour of hard work in wet peat and Nyre's burial words said properly over eleven Wardens, the company sweating and silent, Dellach standing watch facing the way the footprints go; it costs the light and buys something you cannot spend'>>

choices.label: Move before the light goes entirely.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='two hours flat in cold water and then eleven minutes of violence: four Fenkin scouts dead on the path, one of them wearing a Warden's boots and a tally-ring of nine strokes on a thong at his throat'>>

choices.label: Take the tally-ring and get off the path.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the old peat workings, a cut face standing higher than a man, and in it a bog body preserved to the eyelashes: hands bound at the wrist, a strip of iron laid in the open mouth, and the peat above it undisturbed for a century'>>

choices.label: Have Ilsabet read the iron in the mouth.
Take the iron and go.
Cover the face and leave the man his iron.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='Ilsabet reading the strip by lamp: dwarf-cut, a pay-tally, one of nine, and the word she translates last is not a number but a rank, the ninth hand, the one that keeps the count for the other eight'>>

choices.label: Make camp while there is light to choose ground.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the dwarf road going under the hill's shoulder: a cut so straight it insults the moor, roofed in places with slabs the size of doors, and every ninth pace a lamp niche cut into the wall at shoulder height'>>

choices.label: Walk the open cut where the sky still shows.
Take the covered gallery where the roof stands.
Back out and rejoin the dyke track at the sluice.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=55 beats='the open cut, a legion milestone at the bend with nine notches cut under the imperial hand and a lamp niche beside it holding a clay lamp with oil in it that has not had time to gum'>>

choices.label: Take the oil; a full lamp is a full lamp.
Leave the niche exactly as you found it.
Duck into the covered gallery instead.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the lamp decanted into your own reservoir, good clean oil, and Kettle pointing out what you already noticed: somebody fills these, on a schedule, and that somebody will notice the level'>>

choices.label: Push on to the camp ground.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the covered gallery, dry and dark and echoing wrong, the roof slabs holding except where a fall has closed the way at the far end; in the fall's rubble something shifts once with a sound like a chair moved in another room'>>

choices.label: Dig through the fall.
Take the crawl on the left of it.
Back out and take the open cut's lamp niche instead.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='an hour of moving stone by hand in the dark, Dellach and Odd at the face, dust in every throat, until the fall gives up a gap you could get a shoulder through and a draught comes out of it that smells of lamp oil and old meat'>>

choices.label: Take the gap while the fall is quiet.
Widen it properly first; do it once, do it right.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='sixty feet of crawl on your elbows with the roof on your back, and then a chamber: nine lamp niches burnt dry, nine hooks, and a body sitting under them in a good southern coat with a Ledger seal still on its breast'>>

choices.label: Take the Ledger seal off the body.
Back out; nine dead lamps is a message and you have read it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='Factor Halloway's own seal in your hand, and the dead man's satchel holding a fair copy of the Kar Duhn pay account with the ninth signature circled twice in a southern ink that does not run'>>

choices.label: Take it and get out into air.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the last camp, a dry hummock in sight of the barrow gate a mile off, nine lamps burning on the gate hooks in daylight for nobody's benefit, and the company's mood the specific quiet of people doing sums they do not like'>>

choices.label: Full watch, no fire, no talking.
Fire, hot food, and a short watch; they need it.
Send Kettle forward to look at the gate.
Break camp and arrive before dawn.
Call it. The moor has beaten better companies.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='a cold camp and a full watch, and at the third hour a file of lamps comes along the dwarf road below the hummock, nine of them, unhurried, and at the head of the file somebody counting aloud in a language that has too many numbers'>>

choices.label: Let it pass and log the hour.
Follow it at distance.
Leave Bram on watch and get an hour's sleep.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='one small fire in a peat pit, hot food, dry socks, ninety minutes of real sleep each, and at the end of it something standing at the edge of the firelight that does not come closer and does not leave'>>

choices.label: Stand to and challenge it.
Douse everything and lie flat until it goes.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the challenge given in the Warden's form, three times, and the shape at the fire's edge answering on the third with a number instead of a name, and then waiting to see whether the company knows what to say next'>>

choices.label: Say nothing more; hold the line and let it go.
Answer it. Give it the next number.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='Kettle back at dusk with a scout's report and a bad colour: the gate stands a hand's width open, the nine lamps are tended, a Warden's shield is nailed to the post as a notice, and there are boot prints going in and none coming out'>>

choices.label: Go in openly at the gate in the morning.
Wait for the next file and go in behind it.
Send her in alone to open the way for the rest.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='the file goes up the causeway at the third hour and the company follows it in at forty paces, moving on the lamp-count, learning the rhythm of it, arriving at the gate with the door still swinging'>>

choices.label: Go in.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='following nine lamps across a black moor at forty paces, close enough to hear the count and the shuffle of a man in the file who is not walking under his own management, and the count is not going up, it is going round'>>

choices.label: Keep silent and follow to the gate.
Take the count up with them and walk in as one of nine.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='the company falling into the file and taking the count, Kettle's voice steady on numbers she learned as a girl, and in eleven minutes of walking in that rhythm you understand what the file is for and what it is feeding'>>

choices.label: Break off at the gate before the count comes round.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=50 beats='camp struck at midnight and the last mile walked in the dark for no better reason than the captain's impatience, the company arriving at the barrow gate grey and short-tempered with the sky just going pale'>>

choices.label: Look at what you came for.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=75 beats='the barrow gate of Kar Duhn: a dwarf-cut arch driven into the hillside, its lintel carved with a door of nine irons, a Warden's shield nailed to the post with the paint scraped off, nine lamps burning on nine hooks, and the great door standing open the width of a hand and no wider, exactly as the dispatch said'>>

choices.label: Go in by the open door.
Send Kettle up the spoil chute and follow.
Have Ilsabet break the mason's postern.
Sit on the gate and watch it for a full day first.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='a day spent watching a door: at the ninth hour two men in Warden cloaks that do not fit them come out, take down three lamps, and go back in, and neither of them uses his hands to open the door'>>

choices.label: Enough watching. Go in by the door.
Go up the spoil chute where nobody counts.
Take the mason's postern.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='a good dry camp in the lee of a gibbet post, and at the third hour the lamps arrive and stop, and a voice begins a count that includes the sleepers by name in the order they lay down, and the ninth name is the captain's'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=55 beats='the iron beam wet, the crosswind arriving in the middle of the third crossing, and the sluice taking two of the company through the gap in less time than it takes to shout, the water going on afterwards exactly as loud as before'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=50 beats='the rope let go in cold that stops thought, the current under the sluice deeper than it looked and going somewhere the dwarves cut, and the moor keeping what it takes without any fuss at all'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=60 beats='the pace kept and the moor's second attempt succeeding: a false floor of root and water, three of the company in past the shoulder, the mule gone, and Kar Duhn still a grey knuckle on a horizon nobody from the Ninth Sword reaches'>>

Take the gang's lamps and pass as the work-file.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the crate opened: a Warden of the second relief patrol, alive, wrists bound in the Compact's knot, blindfolded and counting under his breath in a rhythm the company has heard three times today and never wanted to hear from a human throat'>>

choices.label: Cut him loose, take him with you, and go.
Ask him what he is counting toward.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=60 beats='the crate's lid levered off and the bound Warden inside cut free and carried, dead weight and counting, while Nyre holds his head and tells him the number is wrong, over and over, which is the only argument anyone has'>>

choices.label: Carry him and go on to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='three Fenkin lamps held at Fenkin height and the company poling a ferry down a flooded dwarf gallery in the middle of a work-file that does not look up, learning by watching what the crates are for, where they go, and how often'>>

choices.label: Tie up at the door steps and get off the water.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the deep pay-hall, ankle-deep and echoing: a rack on the far wall holding eight key-irons in eight sockets, a ninth socket empty, the pay-bell on its stand, and the paymaster himself face down across his own table with both sleeves empty from the elbow'>>

choices.label: Turn the paymaster over.
Take the eight irons off the rack.
Read the tally cut into the wall behind the rack.
Ring the pay-bell and see who still answers it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the paymaster turned over: no hands, no violence anywhere else, and inside his coat a confession written in a hand that had to hold the pen in its teeth, saying that the ninth hand must be a hand that signs, that he signed for nine years, and that he stopped'>>

choices.label: Take the confession and the irons.
Take the confession and go straight to the door.
Look for what happened to his hands.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the rack up close: eight key-irons, each cut with a tally, each seated in a socket that is warm, and the ninth socket empty and worn bright, and the whole rack humming very faintly the way a bowstring hums before it is loosed'>>

choices.label: Take one iron and leave the seven seated.
Leave them all exactly where they are.
Take all eight; the Marshal can have the lot.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='one iron lifted out and the rack's hum going up a tone, seven irons taking the strain of the eighth's absence, and Ilsabet saying, quietly and with great precision, that the company now has eleven minutes of the hill's patience and not a second more'>>

choices.label: Go to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the tally cut into the wall behind the rack, kept in nines, going back nine hundred years in nine hands and then further in a hand that is not dwarf work at all, and the last group having eight strokes cut and a ninth begun'>>

choices.label: Stop reading and go to the door.
Read it to the end; there is a name at the bottom.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the chapel of the Compact: nine benches, a wall of tally, and at a clerk's writing desk a courteous grey man in a good coat who stands as the company comes in, greets them as the Ninth Sword by name and by number, and offers the captain the only chair'>>

choices.label: Hear the offer he means to make.
Ask what the Compact actually pays, and to whom.
Put him down where he stands.
Back out and go and find the wheel instead.
Put a lamp against his tally-wall and burn it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='Coren Vale explains the arithmetic like a factor explaining interest: the thing behind the door is not killable and not wakeable while the count holds, eight irons hold the lid, the ninth hand keeps the count and delivers what is owed, and the frontier has been paying that instalment for nine hundred years'>>

choices.label: Let him make his offer, then.
Leave him talking and go to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the offer, made plainly and without threat: Vale is ninety-one years old and tired, the ninth hand's place is vacant on his death, and he will give the company the iron, the ledger, the garrison's back pay and nine years of the frontier's peace for one of the five, named by the captain, today'>>

choices.label: Refuse, and go for the door.
Counter: the company will settle this another way.
Accept, and name one of them.
Accept, and name yourself.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='the counter-offer put to him: the company will close the door properly, all nine irons seated and no hand at all keeping any count, and Vale's face doing something complicated because in ninety-one years nobody has proposed it, and he is not certain it cannot be done'>>

choices.label: Go to the door with his blessing, such as it is.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='Vale does not defend himself, and does not need to: the chapel does it for him, nine benches worth of dust standing up in the shapes of the people who sat on them, and Dellach's first swing going through a grey man's coat and hitting the desk behind it'>>

choices.label: Finish him before the benches close.
Break off and run for the door.
Take him hostage and walk him to the door.
Stand and fight the chapel.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='Coren Vale killed at his own desk in the time it takes to say a number, and the count stopping: not slowing, stopping, everywhere in the hill at once, and in the silence afterwards the sound of eight irons taking a load they were never asked to take alone'>>

choices.label: Run for the door now, while the silence lasts.
Take his tally-book and his ring off the desk.
Wait and see what the count does without a keeper.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='Vale's tally-book and the ninth hand's ring taken off a dead man's desk, the book eleven hundred pages of instalments in nine hands, the last of them his, and the ring warm and sized, unmistakably, for whoever picks it up'>>

choices.label: Take both and go to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the wheel-house under the pay-hall: a dwarf pump the size of a barn, its wheel turning in a race of black water, three of its nine paddles hacked away and a Fenkin crew working on the fourth with axes and no hurry at all'>>

choices.label: Kill the crew and mend the paddles.
Jam the wheel and flood the deep yourselves.
Cross the wheel-race to the door gallery.
Ride the wheel down and see what it drains into.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='a short brutal fight in a loud room and then an hour of carpentry, Dellach and Odd holding a paddle while Ilsabet lashes it, the water in the race dropping a hand's width, the deep staying dry a while longer for whatever that is worth'>>

choices.label: Leave it running and go to the door.
Stay and keep it running; somebody has to.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the wheel jammed with a poleaxe haft and the race backing up in minutes, water going the wrong way through nine hundred years of dwarf engineering and down into the lower hall where the crates are stacked and the work-file is still working'>>

choices.label: Do it and run for the door on the high side.
Do it now, while half the company is still below.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=60 beats='the wheel-race crossed on the axle housing with the wheel turning a foot from the back of your head, nine paddles coming round, the gap between them exactly as wide as a man who does not hesitate'>>

choices.label: Cross one at a time on the count of the paddles.
Cross together and quickly; the crew has seen you.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the breach in the vault wall, and behind it the barrow the dwarves cut into and thought they had merely cut into: a king's chamber with nine attendants seated round a king who is not there, their plaques still legible, their hands all pointing the same way'>>

choices.label: Read the attendants' plaques.
Close the breach with rubble and be done with it.
Go through the barrow to the door gallery.
Take the ring off the empty king's chair.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='nine plaques read in order, and they are not names but offices: the one who counts, the one who carries, the one who signs, and so on to the ninth, which is the one who is owed, and all nine hands pointing at the chamber's inner door'>>

choices.label: Go to the door with that in your head.
Follow where all nine hands are pointing.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=60 beats='two hours of rubble and mortar dust and Dellach's shoulder against a slab, the breach closed as well as five people can close it, and the certain knowledge in everyone that this is housekeeping and not a solution'>>

choices.label: Go on to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='through the barrow's inner chamber toward the door gallery, past nine empty attendant chairs and one that is occupied by something that has been sitting patiently since before the dwarves cut the first gallery, and that does not turn its head as you pass'>>

choices.label: Walk past it without looking and keep walking.
Look at it properly, once, so you know.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the cutting-shop where the irons were made: a cold forge, a tally-die bolted to an anvil, racks of blanks gone to rust, the cutting-orders still pinned to the bench, and a dwarf smith folded up under the bellows with his tools laid out in order beside him'>>

choices.label: Cut a blank into a ninth iron on the die.
Take the tally-die off the anvil.
Read the cutting-orders on the bench.
Light the forge; you need the heat and the light.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='three hours of cold work with a die that wants a striker and a smith, Ilsabet reading the tally-order aloud stroke by stroke while Dellach swings, and at the end of it a ninth key-iron that is nine parts right and one part yours'>>

choices.label: Take it and go to the door.
Cut a second one while the die is set.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=55 beats='the tally-die unbolted and wrapped, forty pounds of dwarf steel that decides what a key-iron says, which Ilsabet points out is either the most valuable thing in the hill or the most dangerous, and is certainly both'>>

choices.label: Carry it and go to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=70 beats='the cutting-orders read off the bench: nine irons commissioned by the legion at the founding, eight to be cut with the holding tally, the ninth to be cut with a name left blank, to be filled in by the hand that would keep the count, and a note that the blank must never be cut twice'>>

choices.label: Take the orders and go to the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=80 beats='the Ninefold Door at the end of everything: dwarf iron in a frame of older stone, nine sockets in a ring, eight of them filled and warm, the ninth empty and worn bright, the metal of the door itself moving very slightly outward and back on a nine-count that the company has been hearing all day without naming, and behind it, patient, enormous, something that is not asleep and is not awake'>>

choices.label: Set the ninth iron in its socket and lock the door.
Draw the eight irons and unmake the Compact.
Take the ninth iron out of the hill entirely.
Open the door a hand's width and look.
Withdraw. This is a Warden matter and a Ledger crime.
Knock, the way you knocked at the gate.
Walk out of the hill and never speak of it again.

choices.label: Walk it, lamps up, and do not stop.
Put out your own lamps and walk it in the dark.
Take the tags out of the boots; somebody's family gets a name.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=failure words=60 beats='two Warden tags lifted out of a pair of boots that were set down neatly by their owner in a place where nothing is neat by accident, and the nine lamps of the gallery going out in order from the far end, and the boots being, on reflection, a place setting'>>

<<FILL role=climax words=80 beats='the ninth iron set into the ninth socket, which takes it the way a lock takes a key, and the door's slow breathing stopping mid-count: eight irons and a ninth, all nine warm, the frame taking up the load, and nothing behind it moving at all for the first time in nine hundred years'>>

choices.label: Break the tally-die so no tenth iron can ever be cut.
Take the keeper's ring; a count still needs a hand.
Get everyone up the stair while it is quiet.
Drive it in crooked so the socket jams forever.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='the tally-die carried back to the cutting-shop and broken across the anvil in four strokes, dwarf steel going in a way dwarf steel is not supposed to go, and Ilsabet gathering the pieces into a sack because she does not trust fragments'>>

choices.label: Go up the stair.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the ninth hand's ring, warm and exactly sized, and the arithmetic laid out plainly on the chapel desk: nine irons hold the lid without a keeper only until something out there decides to test it, and a count kept honestly by somebody who hates the job is the difference'>>

choices.label: Put it on. Somebody has to keep the count.
Leave it on the desk. Nobody in this company signs that.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=70 beats='the ring on, and the count arriving in the back of the skull like a debt schedule read aloud: not a voice, an obligation, nine every nine, and the captain of the Ninth Sword standing in a dwarf chapel understanding the shape of the rest of a life'>>

choices.label: Take the company up the stair.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=75 beats='the decision to unmake the Compact: eight irons in eight warm sockets, nine hundred years of instalments paid by other people, and a company standing in front of the only arrangement anybody has ever managed with the thing behind the door'>>

choices.label: Draw one iron and watch what the door does.
Draw all eight at once and run.
Draw them, then wedge the ring of sockets with the ninth.
Change your mind and seat the ninth instead.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='one iron out, and the door leans a quarter inch outward; two, and the frame's stone begins to sweat; three, and the door speaks, in the paymaster's voice, politely, asking whether the company is here to settle the account or to increase it'>>

choices.label: Re-seat all three and step back from it.
Keep drawing. Finish what you started.
Ask it what it is owed.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='three irons put back into three sockets by hands that are not steady, the door settling with a sound like a held breath let out slowly, and the paymaster's voice thanking the company by name before it stops'>>

choices.label: Get out of the hill.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the ninth iron driven crosswise through the socket ring rather than into it, dwarf iron biting dwarf iron, the whole ring locked into one piece that no hand can draw and no keeper can count: crude, permanent, and not in anybody's orders'>>

choices.label: Leave it wedged and go up the stair.
Test it first; put your weight on the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=75 beats='a hand's width of the Ninefold Door, held open on the poleaxe haft, warm air coming out of it in a rhythm that is not wind, and light on the other side that is not lamplight and has no obvious source'>>

choices.label: Look through it.
Put a lamp through first and watch what happens to it.
Shut it again without looking. Nobody needs to know.
Speak through the gap.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=75 beats='what is behind the Ninefold Door: not a beast in a lair but a hall the size of the hill with something in the far end of it too large to resolve into a shape, and standing in rows in front of it eleven hundred people, in Warden cloaks and Fenkin leather and dwarf mail, all of them counting'>>

choices.label: Shut it and seat the ninth iron.
Shut it and get out of the hill.
Go in for them. Somebody has to.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='a lit lamp set through the gap on the end of a rope and lowered a foot, where it burns steadily for four seconds, and then goes out from the wick down, and then comes back up the rope relit by nobody at all'>>

choices.label: Look through it now that you have to know.
Reach through and take the lamp back.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the door eased shut on nothing seen, the haft withdrawn, the count resuming exactly where it left off, and five people standing in a dwarf gallery having decided together not to know something they will each privately want to know for the rest of their lives'>>

choices.label: Go up the stair.
Withdraw properly and make it a Warden matter.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=climax words=75 beats='the arithmetic from the other side: eight irons hold the lid on their own for as long as nobody tests it, but the ninth is the count, and a count that cannot be kept is a debt that cannot be collected, and the ninth iron is in your pack'>>

choices.label: Wrap it deep and carry it out of the hill.
Seat it after all; a shut door is worth more than leverage.
Carry it out and sink it in the deepest pool on the moor.
Carry it in the open and let them come and ask for it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=70 beats='salt-cloth, oilcloth, the middle of the pack, and Ilsabet's chalk on the flap, and the whole hill's attention arriving and settling on five people who are now, formally, in possession of the ninth hand's instrument and walking out with it'>>

choices.label: Up the stair, and quickly.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the honest option, said out loud in front of the Ninefold Door: this is nine hundred years old, it is a Warden matter and a Ledger crime, and a five-person company with one contract does not get to be the hinge of it'>>

choices.label: Out the way you came in, and no souvenirs.
Out, but take the pay-ledger from the counting room.
Out, and burn the nine gate lamps behind you.
Out, and sell what you know to Corrow instead.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='back up to the counting room for four pounds of paper that the Marshal will read and the Ledger will want burnt, the lamp above the table still lit, and the clerk's alcove behind it with the plaster tally in it going all the way to the ceiling'>>

choices.label: Take the ledger and go.
Take the ledger and the clerk's tally off the plaster too.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=75 beats='four hundred steps up, and the hill has changed its mind about the company: the flights are longer than they were, the stair-shrine's ninth niche is warm again, all nine lamps in the gallery are lit and trimmed, and at the top the great door has come to within a thumb's width of shut'>>

choices.label: Force the great door with everything you have.
Go out up the spoil chute.
Go out by the mason's postern.
Wait for the ninth hour and walk out with the file.
Sit down on the stair. You are finished.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='five people, a poleaxe haft, a Warden's shield as a fulcrum and eleven minutes of the worst work any of them has ever done, the door giving an inch at a time against a pressure that is not weight and not wind and not interested in negotiating'>>

choices.label: Get everyone through the moment it is wide enough.
Hold it and count them through by name.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the spoil chute from the bottom, forty feet of loose scree at an angle that was bad enough coming down, with the sump behind you filling and the lamps in the gallery going out one by one from the far end toward the stair'>>

choices.label: Go up in pairs, slowly, and take the skin off your hands.
Send the strongest up first to haul the rest.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=60 beats='out by the mason's postern into a night with weather in it, the lead seal broken behind you and the corridor beyond it lighting itself politely, one niche at a time, all the way back to the stair, as if showing a guest to the door'>>

choices.label: Get off the hill.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the ninth hour kept in the oil store and then the file forming on the stair below, nine lamps lifted, the count starting, and the Ninth Sword walking out of Kar Duhn in the middle of it with the rhythm right and nobody's hands where they can be seen'>>

choices.label: Break off at the gate and get clear.
Stay in the file to the end of the count; it is only nine.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the Barrow Moor at dawn with the hill behind and Gallowmere half a day ahead, the company carrying whatever it decided to carry, and Nyre asking the question that has to be answered before anybody speaks to a Warden: what is it we are going to say'>>

choices.label: Straight to Gallowmere and the Marshal.
Two days in a shepherd's bothy first; they are spent.
Put it to the company as a company. All five voices.
Round the town and south with what you carry.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=rising words=65 beats='two days in a shepherd's bothy with a peat fire and nobody's watch to keep, Kettle sleeping eleven hours, Dellach's hands coming back, Ilsabet writing everything down twice in case one copy burns, and the whole company remembering how to be people'>>

choices.label: Walk into Gallowmere on the third morning.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the company council on a wet hillside: Dellach for the Marshal and the record, Nyre for the Ledger hearing and the naming of Halloway, Kettle for the road south, Ilsabet for whichever choice keeps the fewest copies of the truth in the fewest hands'>>

choices.label: Take it to the Marshal, all five names on it.
Take it in and let the record decide it, all five names on it.
Let them argue it out and then decide for yourself.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='back to the gate for the lamp-keeper's boy, which is a promise made in a lamp gallery in front of witnesses and written in Nyre's book, and which means going back up a hillside the company has just spent everything to leave'>>

choices.label: Go in at the postern and get him out.
Call him out from the gate and wait one hour, no more.
Go in by the great door because it is faster.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=75 beats='Gallowmere in the rain again, and everybody waiting: the Warden's tower with a lamp in the window, a Ledger coach outside the counting house with southern horses, the Rooks in the muster yard pretending not to watch the gate, and a woman at the shrine who has a son under that hill'>>

choices.label: Report to Redd, on the record, in full.
Go to the Ledger hearing and name Halloway.
Write the report the Wardens will read in fifty years.
Go back up the hill for the keeper's boy before anything else.
Tell the boy's mother the truth before you tell anyone else.
Say the minimum, take the fee, and be gone by dark.
Hear Corrow's price for your silence and your maps.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the boy's mother at the road shrine, told the truth in a wet street by a captain who has been rehearsing it for two days and gets it wrong anyway, and who finds out that she already knew, and has known since midsummer, and has been lighting candles in nines'>>

choices.label: Take her with you to the Marshal.
Stay with her until the candle burns out.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=75 beats='Warden-Marshal Ansel Redd reads it twice, all of it, without once asking a question, and then sets it down and asks the only ones that matter: what is shut, what is loose, and what is in the company's pack'>>

choices.label: Ask for the Warden charter and a standing writ.
Hand over the ninth iron with the report.
Keep the iron, and have him write to the Deep Road wardens.
Put Vale's book on the table and let him decide.
Tell him the door is shut and leave the rest out.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=75 beats='the written report, which will outlive everyone in the room: dated, signed by five hands, sealed to the Warden archive, and requiring the captain to put down in plain words exactly what was done to the Ninefold Door and by whom'>>

choices.label: Write that the company now keeps the count.
Write that the door is open and how far.
Write that three irons were drawn and reseated.
Write that the sockets are wedged and ask for masons.
Write that the company did not go through the door.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the Ledger hearing convened in the counting room with three factors from the south and Halloway sitting at the end of the table taking his own minutes, and Nyre standing up as a sister of the Reckoning to say that the account is not what the account says'>>

choices.label: Testify in full, everything, on the record.
Testify, and hand the Ledger the iron as surety.
Withdraw the accusation for what he is offering.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=completion words=90 beats='the ninth iron kept, wrapped, and entered on the record as company property held in trust; Redd's letter going south to the Deep Road wardens over his own seal; the Compact's count unkeepable at Kar Duhn for the first time in nine hundred years; and Vale's book open on the Marshal's table at the page that lists eight more doors, the nearest of them under the mountains at the far end of the Deep Road, with a date against it that is this winter'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=75 beats='the writ of salvage upgraded to a Warden charter with a standing commission and a company seal, the Ninth Sword entered in the Marshal's book as a name rather than a hire, and a first order under it that reads, in Redd's hand, hold the hill and report the hour of every lamp'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=70 beats='the ledger delivered, the ninth iron handed across a Warden's table and locked in a Warden's strongbox, sixty crowns paid in full and the hazard added without argument, and a door under the Barrow Moor that is shut tonight and will be shut in the morning'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=75 beats='eleven hundred pages of instalments in nine hands laid on a Warden-Marshal's desk, which makes it his problem and his career and no longer the company's, and Redd reading the last twenty pages with the slow attention of a man understanding that his own predecessor signed one of them'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=75 beats='Factor Halloway named to his face in front of three southern factors, the ninth signature matched to his order-book by Nyre in open hearing, and a Ledger house discovering that its frontier accounts have been settled in people for eleven years by a man who kept excellent records'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=70 beats='a socket ring locked into one piece by a ninth iron driven crosswise, reported in plain words, and a Warden request going south for masons and a mining engineer, because what the company did cannot be undone by any hand and also cannot be trusted by anybody who knows how metal ages'>>

<<FILL role=completion words=70 beats='a promise kept: in by the postern at dusk, the lamp gallery found empty and all nine lamps lit, the boy discovered asleep in the oil store where he had been hiding for two days, and carried out over Dellach's shoulder into weather that has never felt better to anybody'>>

<<FILL role=discovery words=70 beats='a short honest report that says the door is shut and stops there, the fee paid, the company thanked, and four people who each know that a decision was made in a dwarf gallery to leave nine hundred years of arithmetic out of a Warden's file'>>

<<FILL role=discovery words=70 beats='the ninth iron handed to the Ledger as surety and entered in its register under a number, which is the safest place on the frontier and also the one place the Compact has always been able to reach, and a receipt in the company's hands that will be worth exactly what the paper is'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='written down in a Warden file in the captain's own hand: the door is shut, all nine irons seated, and the count is kept by the captain of the Ninth Sword, who will be at Gallowmere every ninth night for the rest of a life that now has a schedule attached to it'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the truth entered in the record to the inch, the tower emptied within the hour, Gallowmere's evacuation order posted by noon, and a company that did the honest thing sitting in the muster yard watching a frontier town load its carts because of a hand's width of open door'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='three irons drawn and reseated, written down exactly like that, and a Warden clerk copying it out twice while Redd asks the question nobody in the room can answer: whether a socket that has been emptied once holds the same as a socket that never has'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='a file that says the company reached the Ninefold Door, described it accurately, touched nothing, and came out, which is the most defensible sentence in the Warden archive and the one the Ninth Sword will be asked about in every taproom for nine years'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='sixty crowns for the ledger, no questions invited and none asked, and the company out of the gate before dark with the money split five ways and an understanding between them that whatever is under that hill is now officially somebody else's arithmetic'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the maps, the route, the lamp hours and the company's silence sold to the Rooks for two hundred crowns and a promise, and a spring in which the Rooks go up to Kar Duhn with eleven people and nobody at all comes back to complain about the price'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='Gallowmere skirted at a distance and the Ledger road taken south with the pack still packed, no report, no fee, no charter, and a ninth iron travelling further from its socket every day in the luggage of five people who have agreed not to discuss it'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='an argument on a wet hillside allowed to run until it stops being an argument, Kettle going south that afternoon, Nyre to her order, Dellach to the tower alone with his own version, and the Ninth Sword ending not in a vault but in a disagreement about paperwork'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='an afternoon in a road shrine with a woman lighting candles in nines, which is the right place to be and the wrong place to be, and a Warden-Marshal who waited until the fourth hour and then wrote in his file that the company did not present itself'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='the ninth iron hammered in at an angle to jam the socket forever, which works, and which also cracks the socket's stone collar, and a ring of nine that has held for nine hundred years discovering all at once that it is now a ring of eight and a wound'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='eight irons pulled in under a minute and a company running for a stair four hundred steps long, which is a plan that requires the door to open slowly, and the Ninefold Door has been waiting nine hundred years and does not see any reason to be slow about it'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the fourth iron drawn while the paymaster's voice is still being polite, and the fifth, and then no more decisions required of anybody in the gallery, because the arrangement the dwarves engineered nine hundred years ago has concluded and the accounts are being settled in the order they were opened'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the question asked through three empty sockets and answered in full, itemised, with dates, and the answer being a figure that the company is standing inside of, and the door explaining without heat that a debt does not require the consent of the instalment'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='a shoulder put against a wedged door to see whether the work holds, which it does, entirely, right up until the thing on the other side puts its own weight against the same door in the same second out of what can only be described as curiosity'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='one sentence spoken through a hand's width of open Ninefold Door, in common speech, politely, and the reply arriving not as sound but as arithmetic: the company counted, priced, scheduled, and entered against an instalment that falls due immediately'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the door pushed wide and five people walking into a hall the size of a hill to bring out eleven hundred who are standing in rows counting, which is the most defensible decision anybody makes in this story, and which adds five to the rows and changes nothing else at all'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='an arm through the gap to take back a lamp that has been relit by nobody, and the lamp being handed over, properly, into the hand that reached for it, by something that has been waiting nine hundred years for a transaction it did not have to initiate'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the ninth iron sunk in eleven feet of black water in the middle of the Barrow Moor, which solves the problem for one winter, until the frost lifts the peat and a fen-runner's boy finds a strip of warm metal in a drained pool and sells it in Gallowmere for two coppers'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the ninth iron carried openly across the Barrow Moor as an invitation, on the theory that whatever wants it will have to come out into daylight and negotiate, and the discovery on the second night that it does not have to come out at all and never has'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='nine lamps smashed and burning in the gate arch as a gesture on the way out, and the hill's answer arriving not that night but nine nights later, in Gallowmere, in a file that comes up the causeway at the third hour with its own lamps and its own list'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='everything the company learned under the hill sold to Vasse Corrow in a wet muster yard for good coin and no receipt, the commission returned unfulfilled, and a Rooks banner going up the causeway a week later with eleven people under it who were told the easy version'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the plaster tally chiselled off the alcove wall because it is evidence and evidence wins arguments, which takes eleven minutes, which is eight minutes longer than the clerk's own arrangement with whatever comes to read his wall on the hour'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='a captain sitting down on the two hundredth step because the legs have finished arguing, and a company that will not leave without its captain, and a stair that has been getting longer all evening and is in no hurry whatsoever'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the great door held on a shield-fulcrum while five names are called through it in order, which is exactly the arrangement the shield's dead owner scratched a warning about on its inside face, and the fifth name being answered from behind the door in the captain's own voice'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='the strongest sent up the chute first to haul the rest, which puts one set of hands at the top and four sets of boots on forty feet of scree that has been waiting all day to move, and it moves while the sump behind them is still filling'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the file stayed with to the end of the count, because it is only nine and the rhythm is easy and the company is nearly out, and the ninth number arriving on the causeway in open air with the moor visible and the count starting again from one without any gap at all'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='the great door taken because it is faster and the boy needs an hour of daylight, and the door being wide enough for one and then not wide enough for anybody, and a company that keeps its promise as far as the threshold and no further'>>

<<FILL role=failure words=70 beats='Kettle's report from the causeway: the Rooks in the yard, a Ledger coach at the counting house, and eleven Warden cloaks at the gate that do not fit the men wearing them, and a company walking into Gallowmere anyway because where else is there to walk'>>

ending.title: Who Was Waiting at the Gate

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='the causeway into Gallowmere in rain that has not stopped since the company left, the stockade in front of you, the Warden's tower lamp lit at the wrong hour, and a coach with southern horses standing outside the counting house with its curtains drawn'>>

choices.label: Walk in openly, up the middle, in your own colours.
Send Kettle ahead to see who is waiting at the gate.
Go round to the Ledger's back gate and be quiet about it.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=65 beats='Kettle back from the gate in eleven minutes with a scout's list: the Rooks in the muster yard doing nothing badly, a Ledger clerk taking names at the counting house door, and eleven Warden cloaks on the gate that do not fit the men inside them'>>

choices.label: Walk in anyway; there is nowhere else to walk.
Wait for full dark and go in over the stockade.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=choice words=70 beats='the Warden's anteroom, wet cloaks steaming on the pegs, the report copied fair in Ilsabet's hand and read once more while a clerk pretends not to watch the pack that has not left the captain's shoulder since the hill'>>

choices.label: Go in and give it to Redd straight.
Ask for the Ledger factor to be present when you speak.
Leave the fair copy with the clerk and walk out of town.

nodes.body: <<FILL role=failure words=65 beats='a fair copy of everything left on a clerk's desk with the company's five names on it and no witness to its handing over, and a Warden-Marshal reading it eleven days later, by which time the coach with the southern horses has been back to the counting house twice'>>
